title: smart-routing-fallback-incident-breadcrumbs-ivy-chen
content:
Incident: regional failover + fallback routing anomalies (notes / breadcrumbs)
Owner: Ivy Chen (personal scratchpad)
Summary:
- During a traffic spike on 2026-02-18 we observed an increase in 502/504s and a set of requests being routed to BACKUP variants incorrectly (backup model in eu-west instead of us-west) despite client region hints. This doc is my working/debugging notes, commands tried, log snippets, hypotheses, and next steps.

Timeline (local time UTC):
- 2026-02-18 14:03 - Alerts: p95 latency for /v1/generate (us-west) > 1200ms, error rate spike from ~0.2% -> 6%.
- 2026-02-18 14:05 - Canary fallback kicked in for some routes (policy: latency fallback -> model-legacy-quantized).
- 2026-02-18 14:07 - Observed ~200 requests routed to eu-west-dedicated pools (unexpected).
- 2026-02-18 14:10 - SRE manually scaled up us-west pool; partial recovery by 14:25.
- 2026-02-18 15:00 - Postmortem ticket created: INF-512.

Reproduction steps (what I ran):
1) Grabbed sample request id list from logs (minimized to reproducible set):
   - request ids: rq_20260218_14_07_{a..f} (see INF-512 logs)
2) Replayed single request via curl to the API gateway (from my laptop in us-west):
   curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $REPL_KEY" -H "X-Client-Region: us-west" -d '{\"prompt\":\"hello\"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
   -> response: 504 Gateway Timeout after ~10s (gateway), no backend trace id in headers.
3) Hit health endpoints for routing service on control-plane and data-plane nodes:
   kubectl -n routing logs svc/routing-controller-0 --since=15m | grep rq_20260218_14_07_a
   -> routing-controller showed policy evaluation success but route decision sent to cluster eu-west-1a (expected us-west-2a).
4) Query routing decision cache snapshot:
   curl -s "http://routing-proxy:8080/decisions?request_id=rq_20260218_14_07_a" | jq .
   -> decision: {\"cluster\":\"eu-west-1a\",\"policy\":\"latency_fallback\",\"reason\":\"fallback_to_lower_cost\"} (note: jq output truncated here in notes)
5) Checked KV cache TTLs and prefix cache metadata for the user key:
   redis-cli -h cache-1.get.redwood TTL user:prefix:abc123 -> 120 (s)

Error snippets copied from router logs:
- [2026-02-18T14:07:12Z] routing-controller INFO evaluatePolicy(req=rq_20260218_14_07_a): latency_history=[320, 480, 1100]ms -> fallback triggered
- [2026-02-18T14:07:12Z] routing-controller DEBUG selectCluster: candidates=[us-west-2a(us:0.6), eu-west-1a(eu:0.9)]
- [2026-02-18T14:07:12Z] routing-controller WARN fallbackDecision: selected eu-west-1a reason=cost_score_low
- [2026-02-18T14:07:14Z] proxy ERROR upstream_connect_timeout id=rq_20260218_14_07_a cluster=eu-west-1a
- [2026-02-18T14:07:14Z] gateway ERROR no_backend_trace_id request_id=rq_20260218_14_07_a

What I checked (quick list):
- Capacity metrics: us-west pool was at 92% GPU utilization at 14:05; autoscaler didn't trigger until 14:10 (config says threshold 85%). Possible autoscaler lag/bug.
- Routing policy config: latest rollout for latency_fallback was applied 2026-02-10 (rollout config references cost weights and region penalty).
- Recent config changes: PR #789 changed fallback cost weights (merged 2026-02-15).
- DNS & peering: No packet loss between gateway and eu-west; tcpdump showed normal RTT.
- Model compatibility: selected backup model variant (legacy-quantized) should be available in us-west, but routing decision bypassed it.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Policy scoring change (PR #789) unintentionally increases cost weight for us-west vs eu-west during high latency, causing fallback to pick eu-west even when local capacity exists. (High confidence)
2) Autoscaler misconfiguration/bug: threshold vs cooldown mismatch meant us-west didn't scale fast enough, pushing policy to choose alternate region. (Medium confidence)
3) Stale cache or race in decision cache causing cluster selection to use outdated cost scores (lower confidence).
4) Gateway routing proxy bug: lost backend trace id and didn't retry correctly on local fallback path (possible contributor to 504s). (Medium confidence)

Commands tried (debugging):
- kubectl -n serving get hpa,deployments -o wide --selector=pool=us-west
- kubectl -n routing logs --since=30m routing-controller-0 | grep latency_fallback
- curl "http://control-plane:8080/configs/latency_fallback" | jq . > /tmp/latency_fallback.json
- git log --pretty=oneline --abbrev-commit --grep="fallback" -- path/to/policy/scorer
- redis-cli MONITOR (short window) to watch decision cache writes during replay
- curl -v "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" with and w/o X-Client-Region to compare outcomes

Observations while digging:
- During the spike, control-plane evals showed fallback reason set to "cost_score_low" rather than "capacity_exhausted". That indicates the policy actively preferred lower cost region, not strictly capacity-based fallback.
- The cost scoring function now includes a penalty term that scales with latency percentiles and an EC2 spot-price factor (PR #789). During temporarily elevated latency, that term can overweight region locality.
- Autoscaler logs show scale-up event at 14:09 but the new nodes weren't ready until 14:14 (normal boot time). We had a 5–9 minute window of underprovision.

Immediate mitigations attempted (notes):
- Reverted live rollout of the new cost weight (rolled back partial feature flag) at 14:20 — observed routing decisions switch back to us-west for subsequent test replays.
- Increased HPA target to be more aggressive temporarily (15m window) to prevent repeated fallback while we investigate.
- Added temporary shim in routing-controller to prefer local region when client provides X-Client-Region header (short-term emergency override).

Next steps (actionable):
- Follow up PR to adjust cost_score weights: revert spot-price term until we have better smoothing (owner: Noah, due 2026-02-25).
- Add unit/integration tests to verify region-preference invariants in latency_fallback scorer (owner: Ivy / Ethan, due 2026-03-05).
- Investigate autoscaler cooldown and node boot time: quantify tail latencies for new nodes and consider aggressive warm pool (owner: SRE/Maya, due 2026-02-28).
- Audit decision cache writes: ensure scoring values are fresh and not using stale TTLs (owner: Ivy, due 2026-02-24).
- Postmortem draft (INF-512) - include timeline, root cause candidate, mitigations, follow-ups.

Loose notes / hypotheses to check later:
- We should check whether billing/cost dashboards show spot price spikes correlated with region choice.
- Confirm whether clients without X-Client-Region are particularly affected (maybe default region mapping is wrong).
- Consider adding an explicit fallback policy type: capacity_only vs cost_aware, and avoid cost_aware for latency-sensitive endpoints.

Artifacts to attach to INF-512 (links / logs):
- routing-controller logs 2026-02-18 14:00-14:30 (S3 path: s3://redwood-logs/routing/2026/02/18/)
- control-plane-config dump: /tmp/latency_fallback.json (attached to ticket)
- autoscaler events: k8s events & cloud provider scaling logs (linked in ticket)
- replay scripts used: https://github.com/redwood-inference/traffic-replay/tree/incident-20260218

My immediate notes for follow-up:
- I left the emergency override in place for now but plan to remove once PR revert is live and autoscaler changes validated.
- Double-check that the emergency override is scoped to affected customer routes only (not global).
- Sync with SRE tomorrow 09:30 PST to review HPA/scale timings.

Raw snippets / CLI output (copied verbatim):
> routing-controller WARN fallbackDecision: selected eu-west-1a reason=cost_score_low details={cost=0.21, capacity_score=0.71, latency_penalty=0.45}
> proxy ERROR upstream_connect_timeout id=rq_20260218_14_07_d cluster=eu-west-1a
> kubectl get hpa -n serving
NAME                REFERENCE             TARGETS         MINPODS   MAXPODS   AGE
model-pool-us-west  Deployment/model-pool  92%/85%         3         24        12d

If anything above is unclear ping me in #ops-incident or drop a note on INF-512. This is a living scratchpad — will update as I validate hypotheses and post the postmortem draft.

-- Ivy
